item.title: Amish Christmas Cookie Tour in Lancaster — Sat Nov 21 — Amish Farm and House
item.description: Interact with Amish families in their homes and learn about their heritage while sampling homemade cookies. This holiday season, make new friends, learn new recipes, and create memories to last a lifetime. Take a step away from the stress of the holidays, slow down, and let us take you on a relaxing and festive journey. We will visit three authentic Amish homes to sample homemade Christmas cookies. You’ll leave with an appreciation of another culture, along with recipes and cookies to take home and enjoy. Dad doesn’t need another tie, and Mom doesn’t want another gift card. Spend time with your loved ones this holiday season; join us for our Christmas cookie tour! IMPORTANT: Please indicate at the time of booking if you are traveling with another party, so that we can do our best to ensure you travel together. Our buses hold a maximum of 14 passengers. item.description:

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Sat Nov 21, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Thanksgiving Day Tour with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Thu Nov 26 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
What better way to relax before “Crazy Uncle Harvey” arrives and the feasting begins on Thanksgiving Day. Enjoy a ride on a 50cc scooter to visit 19th-century covered bridges with an experienced guide. This tour offers exceptional views of the countryside, including Amish farms and schoolhouses, as well as an insightful look at one of Lancaster County’s oldest covered bridges. This tour will give you a uniquely exciting way to get back in touch with historic Pennsylvania. Itinerary Duration: 2-3 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of two of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges A ride through Lancaster’s backcountry road during the loveliest time of year.
Each year is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you!

item.title: Evening Compline — Fri Nov 27, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: We the People First Friday: McCaskey Combined Choirs — Fri Dec 4, 6:30 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Celebrate the vibrant sound of the J.P. McCaskey High School Combined Choirs in this free concert at the Ware Center in Lancaster. The ensemble, made up of the McCaskey Vocal Ensemble and McCaskey Voices of Freedom, will present a diverse program featuring both accompanied and a cappella choral music.
To complement the evening’s art exhibit, the choirs will perform music from African culture, showcasing the students’ versatility and the range of musical styles they study throughout the school year, including both sacred and secular music.
As J.P. McCaskey High School approaches its celebration of 90 years of choral music in Lancaster, come support these talented student singers and experience an evening of music, culture, and community.

item.title: Advent Masterworks for Trumpet and Organ — Fri Dec 4, 8:00 PM — First Reformed Church
item.description:
First Reformed Church of Lancaster will host a free 30-minute concert, “Advent Masterworks for Trumpet and Organ”. The performance features acclaimed local musicians Larry Hershey on organ and Doug Albert on trumpet. The carefully curated program spans seasonal masterworks and festive arrangements: J.S. Bach: A brilliant transcription of the fourth movement of Bach’s masterly cantata, “Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme” Hans-André Stamm: A spirited, uplifting march on the Advent carol “Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme” Christina Harmon: A beautifully textured arrangement of “O Come, O Come, Emmanuel” Marc Cheban: A grand, solo organ performance of “Grand Fantasia on Joy to the World,” performed by Mr. Hershey Maurice André: A brilliant finale featuring Mr. Albert on the piccolo trumpet on “Gloria in excelsis Deo.”
Event Details: Date: Friday, December 4 Time: 8:00 PM (30-minute duration) Location: First Reformed Church, 40 E. Orange St., Lancaster, PA AdmissionFree and open to the pub

item.title: Strasburg Holiday Home Tour — Sat Dec 5, 10:00 AM — First Presbyterian Church
item.description:
Get in the Christmas spirit, enjoy historic homes, and get some ideas for decorating your own! The Strasburg Heritage Society’s 15th annual Holiday Home Tour!
The homes on this year’s tour are all at least a century old, and some are much more. Half of the homes will be in town, within easy walking distance of each other, while the other half showcase wonderful properties all around the Strasburg vicinity. At our Event Center (First Presbyterian Church, 101 S. Decatur Street), tour tickets, lunch, craft vendors, and fresh holiday greens will be available. You are welcome to visit the Event Center even if you don’t purchase a ticket for the tour.
Tickets will cost $30 on the day of the tour, but can be purchased anytime from November 7 to December 4 for $25. Advance tickets can be purchased in person at Main Street Antiques (2 W. Main St.) or Speckled Hen Coffee (141 E. Main St.), as well as online at StrasburgHeritageSociety.org under the Events tab.

item.title: Photos with Krampus at Lancaster Cemetery — Sat Dec 5, 12:00 PM — Lancaster Cemetery
item.description:
Visit the Lancaster Cemetery for its ” Photos with Krampus” fundraiser! Stop by Lancaster Cemetery for holiday photos with Krampus, a horned creature who punishes those who misbehave at Christmastime! Why not have a unique photo for this year’s holiday card?
Suggested donation is $10 for a few poses with (or without!) your pal Krampus. Visitors should bring their own cameras. Volunteers will be on site to assist. This event is first-come, first-serve. Photo set-up may be outdoors this year. Proceeds go toward maintenance of Lancaster city’s historic Victorian cemetery. Leashed and well-behaved pets are welcome. All proceeds benefit The Lancaster Cemetery 501c13 non-profit in preserving, maintaining, and promoting the historic grounds and caretaker house.

item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Nov 25, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
